# v0.27.0-rc8 — summary quality: fleet-proven defaults, summaries that see the middle, stemmed recall, larger leaves

**RELEASE CANDIDATE — not GA.** This prerelease enters the RELEASE-READINESS-V1 gauntlet
(bench/specs/RELEASE-READINESS-V1.md) at this tag: the all-tools live matrix bound to `hermes-lcm-x v0.27.0 (15 tools)`
(A); a P0/P1 sweep of the `v0.26.2`→rc diff, including upgrade from and rollback to v0.26.2 (B); a 30+ turn live host
soak with a committed compaction, 0 loss, 0 duplicates, 0 truncated level-3 nodes (C); the scorecard against
pre-declared bars: recall flips vs the previous GA, facts kept, the OFF QA rows, latency (gauntlet cells max ≤ 145 s) and,
added for rc3 (#1128), a per-message wait replay cell (D); and 24 h or more on the reference agent: max ≤ 120 s, per-message
wait bars and p90 at or below the previous GA's on the same route, on LCM-X-owned time (the spec's D5 row, rc3 and rc5).
Phase B sweeps the full `v0.26.2`→rc diff on every respin.

GA follows only when the receipts are green; the GA tree is this tree plus the `v0.27.0` release-notes file. **rc8
respins rc7** with one fix that the full-diff Phase B sweep at rc7 found (below). rc7 respun for one fix from the rc6 sweep, rc6 for two fixes from the rc5 sweep,
rc5 for a stop-line attribution fix, and rc4 and rc3 for #1139 and #1123.

Minor release on top of `v0.26.2`, including the `v0.26.1` and `v0.26.2` fixes. Theme: **summary quality**, built as a
four-layer compaction architecture: (1) old tool output goes first, externalized and replayed as stubs that name the
read-back call; (2) DAG summaries that now see the middle of long messages; (3) deterministic re-insertion of the
objective, the LCM note and the user's current request; (4) lossless, searchable history with stemmed recall.

**The defaults now match the configuration the managed deployment has run on every profile for weeks**, except that a
leaf summary now reads up to 24,000 tokens of history instead of 8,000 (#1123), which managed profiles take with their
v0.27.0 pin. Most users will notice that compaction starts later (at 75% of the window instead of 35%) and that old
tool output is externalized by default. To keep the old behaviour, set the keys listed under **Upgrade**.

- No tool name or count changed (15 tools); `LCM plugin loaded` and every `lcm_*` name are unchanged. Two dormant tools
  are no longer advertised under defaults (see #1013 part 2).
- No new `LCM_*` setting except `LCM_RECALL_FTS_ANCHOR` (default on, embeddings-on only) and `LCM_SQLITE_MMAP_SIZE` (default unchanged).
- **Store:** `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 5. The stemmed full-text index is a droppable side table that a background backfill
  builds; doctor and status report it, and `/lcm doctor repair apply` re-creates it.
- No change below deletes a stored raw row. This release never moves a deployed pin by itself.

## Upgrade

**Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is required** (#1080). `plugin.yaml` declares `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.3"`, the same floor as
the catalog entry. On Hermes 0.21.2 or older, Hermes skips the plugin and uses its built-in compressor, and the existing
LCM-X database is left untouched. Upgrade Hermes first. The reliability nightly tests the floor host, 0.21.3.

**Hermes 0.21.5 or newer is recommended.** On 0.21.3 and 0.21.4, a compaction right after a tool call can make Hermes send
"tool did not complete" notices in place of that turn's results; the results stay stored and recallable (#1094).

**New defaults.** #1013 sets the first seven to the values the managed profiles already run; #1119 and #1123 set the
last three (managed profiles take those with their v0.27.0 pin):

| Setting | v0.26.x | v0.27.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` | `0.35` | `0.75` |
| `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_COUNT` | `32` | `24` |
| `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS` | `0` (no cap) | `24000` |
| `LCM_THRESHOLD_FULL_SWEEP_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_EXTERNALIZATION_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_ACTIVE_REPLAY_STUBBING_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_TEMPORAL_ROLLUPS_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT_MS` | `60000` | `120000` |
| `LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS` | `20000` | `24000` |
| `LCM_LEAF_TARGET_MAX_TOKENS` | `12000` | `2000` |

- The first-sight stub threshold stays 10,000 tokens. Embeddings stay off; managed deployments turn on the local provider.
- A threshold inherited from Hermes `compression.threshold` is raised to at least `0.75` (a bare Hermes install seeds
  `0.50`); `/lcm status` shows the source `config_yaml:compression.threshold(floored)` with a config warning. Set
  `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` or `lcm.context_threshold` to go lower; neither is floored.
- `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_COUNT=0` now means no fresh tail, whatever `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS` is.

**Rollback:** to `v0.26.2`, plugin only, unless a survival fit on this store projected rows or its projection count is
unknown; then roll back plugin-only to `v0.27.0` or later, or stop Hermes and move the database (with `-wal` and `-shm`)
aside first. `/lcm doctor` names the floor for each store (#919, #966). v0.26.2 ignores `FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH`: after a
rollback with the local provider, run `/lcm embed warmup` or expect full-text-only recall. If you set
`LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS=24000` for v0.27.0, set it back to `8000` when rolling back: v0.26.2 has neither the 2,000-token
summary cap nor the 120 s default timeout.

## Changes since v0.26.2

### Since v0.27.0-rc2 (rc3 to rc8, newest first)
- **rc8: user rows take the projection mark too, but only as the last resort.** During a summary outage, a long tool turn could still stay over the window by the size of its user message, because the second pass never marked user rows (#916 keeps the request readable); the host's overflow retry did not recover it, and v0.26.2 fit. When marking every eligible tool result and assistant row still leaves the list over the survival-fit budget (the window less its reserve), a last pass now replaces user rows of at least 256 tokens and at most 2,400 stored characters with the projection mark, as v0.26.2 did; while the list can fit without it, user rows keep their #916 form. (#1233)
- **rc7: the second survival pass also marks short assistant rows.** During a summary outage, a long tool turn whose assistant rows each held at most 2,400 characters could stay over the window, because the rc6 pass marked tool results only; the host's overflow retry did not recover it, and v0.26.2 fit. The pass now also replaces assistant rows of at least 256 tokens and at most 2,400 stored characters with the projection mark, as v0.26.2 did; user rows kept their #916 form (rc8, above, adds them as the last resort), and nothing changes when the first pass fits. (#1227)
- **rc6: two regressions against v0.26.2, found by the full-diff Phase B sweep at rc5.**
  - A survival fit could not shorten a newest turn made mostly of short tool results (each at most 1,200 characters), so the request stayed over the window. When the list does not fit otherwise, a second pass now replaces stored tool results of at least 256 tokens and at most 2,400 stored characters with the projection mark, as v0.26.2 did; user and assistant rows kept their #916 form (rc7 extends the pass to assistant rows). (#1220)
  - On windows under about 118K, the new default summary-prefix bound could leave a user objective larger than the bound out of the assembled context. With survival fitting on and no explicit assembly cap, an objective that alone exceeds the bound is now kept, without summaries beside it, and the survival fit makes room in the tail. Otherwise assembly is unchanged from rc5; explicit caps keep the #1048 warning. (#1221)
- **rc5: the stop line books the host compressor's wait as `host=`, not `pre=`.** A bypassed child session compacts in Hermes' built-in compressor; that wait read as an LCM-X stall. Attribution only, no behaviour change. (#1155)
- **rc4: small windows no longer compact on every model call.** The default summary-prefix target is one leaf chunk capped at a quarter of the threshold (unchanged from 128k up); a 32k replay went from 360 compactions to 78. (#1139)
- **#1123 (P0): long sessions no longer compact on almost every message.** Past the threshold, a foreground wait writes at most one leaf summary. From 8,000 tokens of history, that leaf freed less than one message adds, so the session stayed over the threshold and compacted again on nearly every message, worst on slow summary routes. The default leaf chunk is now 24,000 tokens; the summary target stays 2,000 tokens (`LCM_LEAF_TARGET_MAX_TOKENS` 12,000 → 2,000). If a summariser refuses a long input, the rescue's last attempt targets 8,000 tokens. Replay on a slow summary route (Track S, managed policy, 120 s timeout, 3 seeds × 2 runs per arm), 8,000 → 24,000 chunk: compactions per 100 messages 87 → 20; mean wait per message 52 s → 10 s; compaction p90 101 s → 64 s; summary-call failures 124 → 0; rows dropped by survival fits 47 → 0; facts kept late .68 → .85. An explicit `LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS` keeps its value. (#1129)
- **#1119: the default summary-call timeout is 120 s** (was 60 s), the host's own default; slow routes' 40–55 s calls timed out at 60 s and stalled compaction. `LCM_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT_MS` and `auxiliary.compression.timeout` override it. (#1121)
- **#1120:** a call that ends at the usable deadline, when the foreground budget or an installed host deadline bound it, is a budget cut whatever its error says, so a host fallback error that masks the timeout no longer opens the circuit. (#1130)
- **#1131 (diagnostics):** a publication-coverage conflict names the missing, extra and double-claimed rows first; a foreground budget stop before the first leaf is logged as that, not as "no eligible raw backlog".

### Defaults and request size
- **#1013 part 2 (#1017): dormant tools hidden.** `lcm_query_state` and `lcm_retrieve` are advertised only when their
  features are on, saving about 1,384 tokens per request. The manifest still declares all 15 tools.
- **#1055: the user/assistant inline floor follows the window:** the larger of 25,000 tokens and a tenth of the
  window (unknown window: the v0.26.2 floor). Tool output and media keep the configured threshold.

### Layer 1 — tool output
- **#1107:** a tool output stubbed at first sight in the turn that crosses the threshold is no longer counted as host
  overhead when the summary prefix is bounded, so later passes keep the stub-first exit. No row was lost.
- **#1075:** `/lcm backup` and `/lcm rotate apply` name the externalized-payload directory to copy with a moved snapshot.

### Layer 2 — summaries
- **#611: summaries see the middle of long messages.** A shared input budget with a legacy retention floor replaces the
  fixed head/tail clip. Measured middle-fact retention: 0/72 → 42/72 on the same material.
- **#899, #947:** a clipped long message or clipped leaf input is summarised, never stored as a verbatim level-3 leaf.
- **#930, #954, #977: a bounded summary prefix** with a known window, keeping the newest summaries without deleting DAG
  nodes; a routine sweep condenses the shallowest eligible depth, and the heaviest only under pressure.
- **#904, #922:** hidden-only compaction leaves the host list unchanged when nothing shrinks; objective-only leaves are skipped.
- **#1012:** a content-filter rejection of one chunk no longer opens the summary circuit (the chunk gets the level-3
  leaf; its rows stay stored); the survival fit reserves the largest host overhead seen, so preflight no longer fails.
- **#1099:** a summary call cut at the foreground budget's deadline after outliving its timeout no longer counts as a
  route failure, so a slow but live summary (the Codex Responses route) no longer opens the summary circuit.

### Layer 3 — what survives compaction verbatim
- **#921, #958, #1048: the user's objective** survives a second assembly in the same turn, a cap, and unanswered tool
  calls (the budget reserves the stubs the final sanitizer adds).
- **#900, #953: the LCM note reaches the model on Hermes** as a plugin system-prompt section, only in sessions LCM
  manages, naming only enabled tools, and never in auxiliary or bypass sessions.
- **#998:** the note names `lcm_recall` first for facts from earlier sessions, and says `lcm_grep` searches this session
  by default. Every agent sees this prompt change.

### Layer 4 — recall
- **#1021, #1035: stemmed full-text recall.** `lcm_recall`'s full-text arm ranks over a porter-stemmed copy of content
  once its backfill completes: LongMemEval-M retrieval (470 scored) R@10 .847 → .873 (paired, p = .0009), for about 22%
  more database, 0.2 ms per write and 72 ms at the median. `lcm_grep` and the other paths keep exact and prefix matching.
- **#1015: `lcm_grep` honours the FTS5 operators its schema advertises** (`OR`, `NOT`, `term*`; `AND` and `NEAR` are
  words); a rejected query retries in the old form, and a multi-term query with no hits retries once as any-term.
- **#1014, #1063, #1108: embeddings keep up by themselves.** A bounded background pass embeds new leaf summaries (and,
  with FastEmbed or a loopback Ollama, message chunks, newest first). FastEmbed registers its profile itself, never
  downloads a model, uses 2 threads and honours `FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH`.
- **#995, #1008:** `lcm_recall` hits carry the host's `event_time`; proactive recall dates a memory by it, not write time.
- **#950:** with embeddings on, the full-text arm's best match is kept in the ranked window (`LCM_RECALL_FTS_ANCHOR`).
- **#1047:** the LIKE fallback fetches its candidate window in one query (a 767K-message CJK store took 146 s before).

### Identity, durability and operations
- **#1000, #959:** a summary carrier re-formed by a survival fit is not stored again as a new row, and a survival
  projection is recognised on a cold resume even when its tool-call arguments quote survival marks.
- **#852:** `/lcm` refuses every subcommand when the session and engine profiles differ.
- **#903, #1084:** `LCM_SQLITE_MMAP_SIZE` sets SQLite mapped reads (use `0` on SD-card hosts); `/lcm doctor` reports
  the linked SQLite version and whether it has the WAL-reset bug.
- **#1080:** the not-active marker moves under `plugin-data/hermes-lcm-x/`; `fastembed` is bounded to `>=0.8.0,<1.0`;
  the plugin no longer writes the host's private hook table when `register_hook` is missing.

## Qualification
- **Independent review.** Every product PR since `v0.26.0` had a merged-head review by a model other than its author
  (the Codex connector on every PR; Claude and Codex cross-reviewed each other's changes), or only text changed after
  it. Exceptions: #1019 (review after merge, #1103) and #1081 (last commit only added `requires_hermes`).
- Full suite at the rc8 head: 7,590 passed, 0 failed (local, Python 3.12); the release PR's CI ran Python 3.11–3.14 and lint.
- The rollback readers in CI include `v0.26.2`, against a store this candidate wrote (#1100). The reliability nightly
  passed its gate on all 5 hosts at the rc base `8bb7b70a` (run 38130276087; 103 cells each, 0 gating).
- Instrument fixes, no runtime change: Track S (#951, #974, #946, #948), Eval-2 (#1064, #1079, #1087), reliability (#1056).
- The rc2 soak's p90 (112.8 s) found #1123, and the rc3 B sweep found #1139. At rc4, A–C and D1–D4 passed, and the soak
  failed its max bar on host-compressor time (124.5 s), which found the rc5 fix. At rc5, every phase passed except Phase B: its
  full-diff sweep (six dimensions, three model families, two-vote verification) found #1220 and #1221. At rc6, the same sweep found #1227, and at rc7 #1233. Reruns at `v0.27.0-rc8`.

## Known follow-ups
- **v0.27.1, from #1123:** prepare leaf summaries in the background and publish them at the threshold, so a foreground wait goes toward zero (#787, first slice); duplicate copies of re-stamped host rows in leaf input (#1124); steps before the first summary call that use or overrun the foreground budget (#1127, #1122); error-path survival fits that leave uncovered rows out of the active context, which stay stored (#1125); `/lcm preset` values (#1126).
- **#1132, #1134:** on a host window under 64k tokens or a summary route under about 30k, the 24,000 chunk can defer compaction (no stub-first exit, no smaller retry for one large message); set `LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS=8000`. (v0.27.1)
- **#1247:** on a host window under 48k tokens (Hermes accepts one only with an explicit `model.context_length` on a local provider), the fresh-tail cap can equal the compaction trigger, so a long run of uniform tool calls leaves most older rows out of both the live context and the summaries; they stay stored and searchable. Set `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS=12000`. (v0.27.1)
- **#1096, #1137:** a slow or hung summary route can spend the 120 s bound with no leaf and no fallback; **#659:** the user carry packet, whose real-host check was inconclusive (accuracy +2 pt, 95% interval −5 to +9). (v0.27.1)
- **#1222:** P3 findings from the rc5 full-diff Phase B sweep: stem-index repair, a bounded repair join, child-bypass budget state, the fallback note's tool filter, the objective scan's copying, the `lcm_grep` schema text, and the doctor `journal_mode` line. (v0.27.1)
- **#1225:** an objective too large for the room left beside the newest turn still overflows the window, as in v0.26.2; v0.27.1 projects it instead. (v0.27.1)
- **#1068:** Hermes' native Responses compaction (`compression.codex_responses_native`) reads LCM-X's threshold and can fire before it. Keep it off with LCM-X until Hermes gates native compaction per context engine. (v0.28.0)
- **v0.28.0, also:** a shutdown that waits for background work (#1086); an identifier index only if Eval-2 shows no harm (#1066); no context engine below the plugin API floor (#1083); what an affected SQLite should change (#1085).

## Benchmark boundary
- Measured in this release: stemmed recall (R@10 .847 → .873, #1035), middle-of-message retention (0/72 → 42/72, #611)
  and compactions per message on a slow summary route (87 → 20 per 100 messages, #1123). The Phase D scorecard runs at
  this tag; the GA notes report its rows.
